flags.gpt_reasoning: For a residential nonpayment pay-or-quit notice, current Georgia law is governed by O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50(a), which requires the landlord to make the statutory demand and provide at least three business days’ written notice to vacate or pay before filing a dispossessory action. Section 44-7-50(a) does not prescribe separate personal, substituted, or mail service methods; O.C.G.A. § 9-11-4 and O.C.G.A. § 44-7-51 concern service of court process/summons, not the pre-suit pay-or-quit notice.
flags.gemini_reasoning: O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50(a) requires a landlord to make a demand for possession before initiating a dispossessory action but does not prescribe a specific method of service. Georgia case law confirms that any method of delivering the demand, including oral notice, is legally sufficient as long as the tenant receives it. The more formal service requirements (e.g., in O.C.G.A. § 44-7-51) apply to the dispossessory summons and affidavit filed with the court, not the initial pre-litigation notice.

federal.applies_when: Covered dwelling: federally backed mortgage loan (Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac) or covered housing program (HUD assistance, Section 8, LIHTC, rural housing, etc.)
federal.effect: During active moratorium periods: 30-day notice required before filing; no fees or penalties for nonpayment during moratorium. Emergency moratorium provisions expired July 2021 but covered-dwelling definition and notice requirements may persist under other federal programs — verify current applicability.

federal.name: SCRA § 3951 (Servicemembers Civil Relief Act)
federal.applies_when: Servicemembers and their dependents occupying a residence as their primary dwelling, where the servicemember's military service materially affects their ability to pay the rent.
federal.effect: During a period of military service, a landlord may not evict a servicemember or their dependents from their primary residence without first obtaining a court order. Court may stay proceedings up to 90 days or adjust the rental obligation. Protection applies when monthly rent does not exceed the annual threshold: $4,954.34/month (2024; formula: 130% of BAH for E-5 with dependents, highest BAH area — adjusted annually by DoD). Landlord must file affidavit of non-military-service before default judgment may enter (50 U.S.C. § 3931(b)(1)). FY23 NDAA amendment: replaced CPI-adjusted fixed-dollar threshold with current BAH formula.

Similarly situated non-protected tenants were treated more favorably, OR discriminatory intent can be shown, OR facially neutral policy has disparate impact
substantive_defenses.note: Federal FHA prohibits discrimination in housing based on protected class. State law may provide additional protected classes and remedies. Discriminatory intent or disparate impact analysis is fact-intensive — specialist review required. grounding_gap: state fair housing case law and protected class details.

elements_confirmed: The tenant is a member of a protected class under the federal Fair Housing Act or Georgia's Fair Housing Law.
The tenant was subjected to an adverse housing action (eviction).
The eviction was motivated by the tenant's membership in the protected class, which can be shown through direct evidence or by establishing a prima facie case that shifts the burden to the landlord.
The landlord's proffered non-discriminatory reason for the eviction (e.g., non-payment) is a pretext for illegal discrimination.
